prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one universal “best” HVAC company for Atlanta — the right choice depends on your home, budget, desired brand/warranty, and how well the contractor installs and supports the system. I can help you pick the best one for your situation. To start, tell me your zip code, the size/age of your home, and the age/brand of your current system. Meanwhile, here’s a practical approach and a short list of what to look for.

How to choose the right company
- Get at least 3 written quotes that include equipment model numbers, matched components, SEER rating, estimated tonnage, and labor costs.
- Verify credentials: Georgia HVAC license, NATE-certified technicians (preferred), proof of insurance, and local permits included in the bid.
- Look for manufacturer-authorized dealers for brands you prefer (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Rheem, etc.) if brand/warranty matters.
- Check reviews: Google, Better Business Bureau, and recent customer photos. Pay attention to installation-related complaints, not just service calls.
- Ask about warranties: compressor & parts, labor, and what voids the warranty (improper installation).
- Make sure they perform a Manual J load calculation and inspect/assess ductwork. Proper sizing and ductwork are the most common causes of poor performance.
- Confirm they’ll pull required permits and dispose of the old unit.

Questions to ask each contractor (short script)
- “Are you licensed in Georgia and insured? Can you provide license number and proof?”
- “Will you perform a Manual J load calculation for my home? Can I see the report?”
- “Which exact model and SEER rating are you proposing, and are all components matched by the manufacturer?”
- “What is included in the installation? (flush lines, new thermostat, condensate, startup, permits, disposal)”
- “What are the equipment and labor warranties? Is there an extended labor warranty option?”
- “Can you provide recent customer references in my area and photos of similar installs?”
- “How long will the installation take and when can you start?”

Red flags
- Very lowball bids that come without a load calc or vague equipment descriptions.
- Pushy sales tactics to sign immediately to “lock a price.”
- Refusal to pull permits or provide a written contract.

Estimated cost and timeline (Atlanta area, rough)
- Typical full-system replacement (mid-efficiency 14–16 SEER): roughly $4,000–$8,000.
- High-efficiency systems (18+ SEER, Trane/Lennox/Carrier top models) often run $7,000–$12,000+.
- Exact cost depends on house size, ductwork work needed, and brand. Install generally takes 1–3 days for a straightforward swap; more if ductwork or structural work is required.

If you want, I can:
- Pull up the top-rated HVAC companies near your zip and list 3–5 reputable options with pros/cons.
- Draft an email or phone script you can use to request quotes.
Tell me your zip code and any priorities (budget, brand, timeline, financing), and I’ll find local recommendations and prepare suggested questions to send them.
